docs.title: Gold Fin Apparel Overview
docs.text:
Gold Fin Apparel is a customizable clothing product line focused on premium shirts that customers can tailor through a variety of selectable attributes. Customers can personalize shirts based on size, style, design, material and color.

Cost is calculated consistently to ensure clear and reliable pricing while enabling flexible product-mix combinations.

docs.title: Gold Fin Apparel User Guide
docs.text: Welcome to Gold Fin Apparel. This guide provides step-by-step instructions for browsing products, customizing your selections, managing your cart, and completing your purchase.

docs.title: Navigating the site
docs.text:
1. Open your web browser and navigate to the Gold Fin Apparel website at www.goldfinapparel.com.

  2. Use the navigation bar at the top of the page to access different sections of the site, including Home, Browse, Cart, Help, and About.

    • Home: Return to the featured products carousel
    • Browse: View all available apparel styles
    • Cart: Review selected items and proceed to checkout
    • Help: Access size charts, shipping information, and return policies
    • About: Learn more about Gold Fin Apparel

  3. Click Browse to start exploring product offerings.

    Browse products by category, price, size, and other filters to find the perfect apparel for you.

  4. Click on any product image or name to view detailed information and customization options.

    You can select from various designs, sizes, colors, and materials to create a personalized item. The product page also displays multiple images, price information, and a detailed description to help you make an informed decision. View Customizing your selection for more details on how to customize your apparel.

  5. Click Add to Cart when you have finalized your selection. You can review and modify your cart before proceeding to checkout.

  6. When you are ready to complete your purchase, click Cart in the navigation bar to review your selected items and proceed to checkout. View Managing your cart for instructions on how to review and modify your cart contents.

  7. Follow the checkout instructions to enter your shipping and payment information, review your order, and complete your purchase. View Completing your purchase for detailed checkout instructions.

  8. After completing your purchase, you will receive an order confirmation email with details about your order and estimated delivery date.

docs.title: Selecting a design
docs.text:
• On the product inspection page, review available designs.
  • Click on the Featured Designs at the top of the page or browse additional designs in the design selector.
  • Each design is displayed with a preview image.

docs.title: Choosing size
docs.text:
• Click the Size button corresponding to your desired size.
  • Available sizes are displayed as selectable buttons.
  • Unavailable sizes are grayed out and cannot be selected.

Size selection

If you are unsure about sizing, consult the Size Charts in the Help section. Size charts are available by product type (T-shirt, Vest, Kimono, etc.).

docs.title: Selecting color
docs.text:
• Click the Color button to view available color options.
  • A color palette or list of available colors appears.
  • Click on your preferred color.

docs.title: Choosing material
docs.text:
• Click the Material button to view material options.
  • Available materials are displayed with texture previews where applicable.
  • Click on your preferred material.

Material compatibility

Not all colors and materials are available for every design and size combination. When you select an option, incompatible choices are automatically disabled.

docs.title: Adding items to your cart
docs.text:
1. After customizing your product selection, specify the desired quantity.
  2. Click the Add to Cart button.
  3. The item is added to your cart and a confirmation message appears.

docs.title: Reviewing your cart
docs.text:
Click Cart in the navigation bar. Your cart displays:

  • Selected items with customization details (design, size, color, material)
  • Price per item and subtotal
  • Total cart value
  • Quantity for each item

docs.title: Changing quantity
docs.text:
1. Locate the item you want to modify in the cart.
  2. Adjust the quantity field or use the quantity adjustment controls.
  3. The cart total updates automatically.

docs.title: Removing items
docs.text:
1. Click Remove next to an item you want to delete.
  2. A confirmation dialog appears.
  3. Confirm the removal. The item is deleted from your cart.

docs.title: Clearing your cart
docs.text:
1. Click Clear Cart in the cart view.
  2. A confirmation dialog appears asking you to confirm.
  3. Click Confirm to remove all items from your cart.

Cart persistence

Your cart is automatically saved to your browser's local storage. If you close your browser, your cart contents are preserved and available when you return.

docs.title: Accessing checkout
docs.text:
1. Review your cart to ensure all selections are correct.
  2. Click the Checkout button.
  3. The checkout page displays an order summary.

docs.title: Entering shipping information
docs.text:
1. In the Shipping Information section, enter:

    • Full name
    • Street address
    • City
    • State or province
    • Postal code
    • Country

  2. Select your preferred Delivery Method:

  3. Standard Delivery: Estimated delivery in 5-7 business days
  4. Express Delivery: Estimated delivery in 2-3 business days

docs.title: Entering payment information
docs.text:
In the Payment Information section, enter:

  • Cardholder name
  • Card number
  • Expiration date
  • CVV (card security code)

docs.title: Reviewing your order
docs.text:
Before completing your order:

  1. Verify all items in your order summary
  2. Confirm shipping address and delivery method
  3. Review itemized costs:
  4. Subtotal
  5. Estimated shipping cost
  6. Applicable taxes

  7. Order total

  8. Verify estimated delivery date

docs.title: Completing the purchase
docs.text:
1. Click the Complete Order button.
  2. Your order is processed and confirmed.
  3. You are directed to an Order Confirmation page displaying:
  4. Order confirmation number
  5. Order details and itemized costs
  6. Shipping address
  7. Estimated delivery date
  8. Next steps for order tracking

docs.title: I cannot select certain options
docs.text:
Issue: Some color, size, or material options are grayed out and cannot be selected.

Solution: Not all combinations of design, color, material, and size are available. Try selecting a different combination.

docs.title: My cart is empty
docs.text:
Issue: Items I added to my cart are missing.

Solution:

  • Check if you cleared your cart accidentally
  • Try clearing your browser cache and cookies, then reload the page

docs.title: Payment is not processing
docs.text:
Issue: My payment is declined during checkout.

Solution:

  • Verify your card number, expiration date, and CVV are correct
  • Ensure your billing address matches your card information
  • Try a different payment method
  • Contact your bank to verify the card is not blocked

docs.title: I cannot complete my order
docs.text:
Issue: The Complete Order button is inactive or not responding.

Solution:

  • Verify all required fields in the shipping and payment sections are completed
  • Ensure your cart contains at least one item
  • Check your internet connection
  • Try reloading the page
  • Use a different browser if the issue persists

docs.title: Installation and Deployment Guide
docs.text:
Installing and deploying Gold Fin Apparel, including frontend, backend, and database configuration.

Prerequisites

Ensure you have the following installed on your system:

  • Node.js and npm (for frontend development)
  • Python 3.9+ and pip (for backend development)
  • Access to an IBM Db2 for z/OS instance

docs.title: Frontend Setup
docs.text:
The frontend is a Vue.js-based single-page application built with Vite.

  1. Navigate to the frontend directory.

    cd frontend

  2. Install all required npm packages.

    npm install

    This command reads package.json and installs all dependencies including:

    • Vue.js 4.6.4
    • Vue Router 4.6.4
    • Vite 5.0.0
    • TypeScript 5.0.0

Optional

Run the development server with hot-reload.

npm run dev

The development server typically runs on http://localhost:5173. You can access the application in your browser and see changes update in real-time.

  1. Create an optimized production build.

    npm run build

docs.title: Backend Setup
docs.text:
The backend is a Flask REST API application that connects to IBM Db2 for z/OS.

  1. Navigate to the backend directory.

    cd backend

  2. Create an isolated Python virtual environment for the project.

    Windows:

    python -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\activate

    After activation, your terminal prompt will show (.venv) at the beginning.

  3. Install all required Python packages.

    pip install -r requirements.txt

    This installs:

    • Flask 3.1.3 — Web framework
    • ibm_db 3.2.8 — IBM Db2 Python driver
    • requests 2.32.5 — HTTP library
    • Additional supporting packages

  4. Configure database credentials by creating or updating backend/src/config/db_credentials.json.

        {
      "host": "<your_db2_hostname>",
      "port": "50000",
      "db_instance": "GOLDDB",
      "protocol": "TCPIP",
      "username": "<your_user>",
      "password": "<your_pass>"
    }

Security

Never commit db_credentials.json to version control. Add it to .gitignore and manage credentials securely in your deployment environment.

  1. Configure backend settings by ensuring backend/src/config/backend_settings.json exists with appropriate application configuration.

        {
      "debug": false,
      "host": "0.0.0.0",
      "port": 5000,
      "log_level": "INFO"
    }

    Adjust these settings based on your deployment environment.

  2. Start the Flask API server.

    python -m src.api

    The API server typically starts on http://localhost:5000. You should see output indicating the server is running.

    Running in Production

    For production deployment, use a production WSGI server such as Gunicorn or uWSGI instead of Flask's development server:

        pip install gunicorn
    gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5000 src.api:app

docs.title: Gold Fin Apparel Release Notes Version 1.0
Overview
docs.text:
Product: Gold Fin Apparel Version: 1.0 Release Date: March 2026

Gold Fin Apparel is a modern e-commerce platform that enables customers to browse, customize, and purchase apparel with configurable attributes including design, color, size, and material. This initial release provides a responsive web interface integrated with a Flask REST API backend connected to IBM Db2 for z/OS.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• Web-Based Apparel Customization Interface — A responsive, Vue.js-powered user interface that enables customers to browse apparel products, configure custom selections (design, color, size, material), and complete orders from any modern web browser.

  • Multi-Attribute Product Selection — Support for apparel products with multiple configurable attributes (style, design, color, size, and material) where attribute combinations influence final product pricing and availability.

  • Product Catalog API — RESTful endpoints providing access to:

  • Apparel product listings with base prices and descriptions
  • Available designs with pricing components
  • Color options with availability indicators
  • Size options with sizing information
  • Material options with texture and pricing data

  • Real-time inventory status

  • Order Management — Core order processing with support for:

  • Creating orders linked to customer information
  • Managing multiple line items per order with unique customization combinations
  • Automatic unit price calculation based on style, design, color, size, and material selections

  • Order validation and confirmation workflows

  • Mainframe Db2 Integration — Direct integration with IBM Db2 for z/OS via Python and ibm_db driver, enabling secure, scalable transaction processing on the mainframe.

  • Customer Information Management — Customer data management with support for multiple delivery and billing locations per customer.

  • Comprehensive Logging and Error Handling — Built-in logging infrastructure with configurable log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) for production monitoring and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Technical Enhancements
docs.text:
• Flask 3.1.3 framework for REST API development
  • Vue.js 4.6.4 with Vue Router for responsive frontend development
  • Vite 5.0.0 build tooling for optimized frontend development and production builds
  • Component-based Vue.js architecture for maintainability
  • IBM Db2 driver (ibm_db 3.2.8) for Python-based database connectivity
  • Python 3.x with comprehensive logging and validation frameworks

docs.title: Frontend Requirements
docs.text: Component Requirement Web Browser Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge (latest stable versions) Network HTTP/HTTPS connection to backend API Node.js (Development) Node.js 20.x or later Runtime Vite-built static assets

docs.title: Backend Requirements
docs.text: Component Requirement Python Runtime Python 3.9 or later Flask Flask 3.1.3 or later Package Manager pip (Python package manager) Virtual Environment venv or virtualenv IBM Db2 Driver ibm_db 3.2.8 and clidriver binaries Operating System Windows, Linux, or macOS

docs.title: Database Requirements
docs.text: Component Requirement Database IBM Db2 for z/OS Connectivity IBM Db2 Connect gateway or direct connection to mainframe Db2 Schema Customer, Product, Design, Inventory, Order, and OrderItem tables Driver IBM Data Server Client (ibm_db Python driver)

docs.title: Available Endpoints (v1.0)
docs.text:
• GET /inventory — Retrieve a complete list of stock sorted by quantity with optional filtering
  • GET /designs — Retrieve a list of all available designs sorted by name with optional filtering
  • POST /order — Add an order to the database and automatically decrement stock

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• No User Authentication — Version 1.0 does not include user authentication or authorization. All API endpoints are publicly accessible.

  • No Payment Processing — Payment processing and payment gateway integration are not included in this release.

  • Limited Order Modification — Orders cannot be modified after submission.

  • Single-User Session Management — No session management for concurrent users. Cart data is stored in browser local storage and not synced across devices.

docs.title: Frontend Components
docs.text:
• Browse — Product catalog browsing with filtering capabilities
  • Home — Landing page with featured products carousel
  • Inspect — Detailed product view with customization options
  • Cart — Shopping cart management with item modification
  • CheckOut — Order review and checkout workflow
  • About — Company information and branding
  • Help — Customer support resources
  • TaskBar — Main navigation component

docs.title: Backend Modules
docs.text:
• API — Flask REST API endpoints and request handling
  • Database — Db2 connection management and data access objects (DAO)
  • Logger — Configurable logging with multiple log levels
  • Order Validation — Order data validation and business logic
  • Configuration — Settings management for database and application configuration

docs.title: Inventory Query Issues
docs.text:
Issue: Empty inventory results returned for valid product IDs.

Workaround: Verify that filter criteria are correctly formatted in request headers and that corresponding products exist in the database.

docs.title: Database Connection Timeouts
docs.text:
Issue: Connection timeouts when connecting to remote Db2 instances.

Workaround: Verify network connectivity to the Db2 host, confirm firewall rules allow outbound connections on the configured port, and check database credentials.

docs.title: Design Selection Errors
docs.text:
Issue: Selected designs show as unavailable for certain color and size combinations.

Workaround: This is expected behavior. Not all designs are available in all color, size, and material combinations. Select alternative options or contact support.

docs.title: Managing Sales Reports
docs.text: Viewing sales reports is an important aspect of managing Gold Fin Apparel, and the reports manager provides valuable insights into customer orders and product performance. You can view reports that show unique orders and quantities by customer and date, and every unique item ordered along with its attributes and the total quantity sold for each item. This can be used to make informed decisions about inventory management, marketing strategies, and overall business performance.

docs.title: Accessing Sales Reports
docs.text:
Prerequisites

Viewing sales reports requires that you have the most recent project repository with the latest updates. You can clone the project repository from GitHub at Gold_Fin_Apparel.

You will also need Zowe Explorer v3.4.2 installed for Visual Studio Code to access the mainframe environment and view the sales reports. You can install the Zowe Explorer extension from the Visual Studio Code marketplace.

For configuring Zowe Explorer to connect to your mainframe environment, see more at Zowe Explorer Documentation.

  1. Open Visual Studio Code and navigate to the Zowe Explorer panel.

  2. Right Click the zosmf file and select Create New Data Set.

    1. Name the Data Set: <USERID>.PROJECT.REPORTS

    2. Select Partitioned Data Set Default

    3. Allocate New Data Set

  3. Right Click the newly created Data Set and select Create New Member. You will need to create two members to store the sales reports.

    1. Name member one: QUERYJCL

    2. Name member two: SQL1

  4. Navigate to jobs/queryjcl, in the Gold Fin Apparel project repository, and copy the contents of QUERYJCL.jcl into the QUERYJCL member you just created.

Note

Update the path in the JCL file to point to the SQL file you just created. The path should be: <USERID>.PROJECT.REPORTS(SQL1).

  1. Navigate to jobs/sql1, in the Gold Fin Apparel project repository, and copy the contents of SQL1 into the SQL1 member you just created.

  2. Save both members and submit the QUERYJCL job to run the SQL query and generate the sales reports.

docs.title: Viewing the Sales Reports
docs.text:
After a job has successfully submitted, you can view the output in the Zowe Explorer panel under the Jobs section. Look for the job you just submitted and click on it to see the details. The output will include the results of the SQL query, which will show the sales reports based on the criteria defined in the SQL1 file.

The sales reports will include the following information:

  • Unique orders and quantities by customer, showing customer ID, product ID, design ID, and total quantity.

  • Sales data by date, showing date, product ID, design ID, and total quantity.

  • Every unique item ordered along with its attributes (size, style, material, color) and the total quantity sold for each item.
